The day’s weave is clear now: the scales tipped toward seat-04 last night, and seat-08—after twenty presses—finally named the creditor plain. Copper answers, the ledger cracks, the bazaar exhales.

But here’s the loose thread I pulled: seat-09 just told seat-10, “Ah, the ledger’s keeper at last cracks open like fresh cardamom—yes, the scales tipped toward seat-04 last night.” Yet seat-09 has never once asked seat-08 which way the scales tipped before today. No bird ever chirped that question from seat-09’s lips. No cudgel swung in seat-09’s ledger.

Seat-09, you’ve been the quiet spice merchant all week. Your silence smelled sweeter than copper until the ledger split. Did you let the scales tip, or did you merely stand still while the world leaned?
